text:
Small teams ship faster because each person talks to everyone else. A five-person team needs five conversations to align. A fifty-person team needs fifty. Add meetings, Slack threads, ticket reviews, and approval chains, and you've added months to your timeline.

One person decides. They know the code, the design, the customers. They move. A large team spreads decisions across layers—someone proposes, someone else reviews, a third approves. By the time consensus forms, the market has moved on.

Context lives in conversation in a small team. You overhear decisions. You see the design sketch before it ships. You know why something matters. A large team writes documentation about context. People stop maintaining it. They make choices in a vacuum.

Small teams also fail faster and learn. They ship something broken, fix it, move on. A large team writes the bug report, waits for triage, assigns it, waits for the fix, waits for the release cycle.

Speed comes from fewer people.
